steps.title: Register Dropbox app with App Folder access and only files.metadata.read
steps.detail: In the App Console, create the app with App Folder access and select only files.metadata.read. Confirm no other scope is enabled and record the app key and secret server-side.
steps.doneWhen: App Console shows App Folder access, files.metadata.read as the only scope, and a redirect URI is saved.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the App Console

steps.title: Implement authorize URL, callback and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization redirect, the callback handler and the token exchange using the client secret on a server, or PKCE for public clients.
steps.doneWhen: Callback code path compiles and exchanges a test authorization code for an access token in a test environment.

evidence.quote: https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code in the
Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

steps.title: Authorize a representative test customer account
steps.detail: Sign into a test Dropbox account that stands in for a customer, approve the app, and capture the access token from the callback exchange.
steps.doneWhen: The test account approves the app and the exchange returns an access token usable as a Bearer token.

evidence.quote: In this flow: The user will be redirected to Dropbox to authorize your app to access their Dropbox data.
After the user has approved your app, they’ll be sent back to your app with an authorization code
Your application exchanges the authorization code for an access token that can be used to make secure calls to the Dropbox API (not shown)
be used by your app in subsequent API calls for that user. It should be passed with the Authorization HTTP header value of Bearer <oauth2-access-token>

steps.title: Test list_folder on the App Folder root
steps.detail: Call list_folder with an empty path for the App Folder root and non-recursive mode. Confirm the response lists names and returns a cursor and has_more. Do not call content download or upload endpoints.
steps.doneWhen: Response contains entries with file or folder names, a cursor, and a has_more flag.
